fullDescription: A dense report deck that actually holds data. An unequal 30/70 split puts a narrow saturated rail down the left carrying identity, one statistic and a pull quote, while the wide field takes a heavy display headline and a genuine eight-row table with a totals rule. Bone and rust, flat fields, tabular figures throughout. Good for estate and operations reports, quarterly reviews, board packs, and any deck that has to survive someone reading the numbers.
prompt:
## Resumo
A dense two-panel report deck: a narrow saturated rail on the left against a wide field holding a heavy display headline and a real eight-row data table.

## Estilo Visual
Apply a flat two-colour report style. Palette: field #F2EFE6, rail and display ink #B7472A (plus 65/30/15% for hierarchy). Typography: 'League Spartan' 900 for display at line-height 0.84 and letter-spacing -0.03em; 'Instrument Sans' 400-700 for all copy, labels and table cells, with labels uppercase at letter-spacing 0.18em. Use font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums on every figure. Deliberately avoid Anton — it is the safe bold-poster default and reads as a stock choice. Colour fields are FLAT: no gradient, no card shadow, no rounded panels.

## Layout e Estrutura

### Cover
Rail: a small inline-SVG four-point star mark, the organisation name as two display lines at 104px in the field colour, a short blurb, and a fine-print line pinned to the bottom. Field: a three-column metadata row at the top (report / season / prepared by, each a small uppercase label over a bold value), then the title as two display lines at about 266px with the second at 30% opacity, a row of three outlined pills, and a two-line summary. Foot line left, page number right.

### Data table
Rail: a three-line display heading at 150px, a short method note, then a rule and one headline statistic at 96px with a caption. Field: a display heading at 118px, a two-line lede, then a REAL table — six columns, eight body rows and a totals row separated by a 2px rule, with uppercase 15px headers over a 2px rule and hairline row separators at 15% opacity. Right-align every numeric column and give the numeric cells 8px of right padding plus the adjacent text column 44px of left padding, or the figure and the note will butt together with no gutter. Check the rail's giant heading against the copy beneath it — that collision is the failure mode here.

### Closer
Rail: a pull quote at 34px in the field colour, attributed with a small uppercase two-line credit. Field: three stacked display lines at 196px with the last at 30% opacity, and a two-line paragraph of concrete next steps beneath. Keep the giant type entirely in the field — letting it cross into the rail collapses the split that makes the deck legible.

## Componentes Especiais de UI

### The unequal rail — A 30/70 split where the narrow side is saturated and never holds display type.
A flat full-height rectangle in the accent colour occupying the left 30% of the stage, with all field content offset to start past it. The rail changes CONTENT type on every slide — identity, then a single statistic, then a pull quote — while its width and colour hold. Confine poster-scale type to the wide field; the rail may carry display type only at a much smaller size. An equal split, or giant type on both sides, loses the whole effect.

### The eight-row table — Actual reading-level density, which is the point of the register.
A real HTML table with a colgroup fixing column widths: a short code, a bold name, three right-aligned numeric columns in tabular figures, and a right-aligned assessment column of plain sentences. Eight body rows plus a totals row set off by a 2px top rule and no bottom border. Header cells uppercase at 15px in the 65% ink over a 2px rule; body rows separated by 1px hairlines at 15%. Write the assessment column as real judgements, not filler — the density is the differentiator and it only works if the content rewards reading.
